In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of doped, poled polyimidies as dielectric materials for MCM-D applications.
the use of poled polymeric films in MCM-D applications, both for noninvasive measurement of electric fields and for light guiding in MCMs.
the development of polyimide-based dielectric layers for MCM-D applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electro-optic properties and optical transparency of poled polyimidies make them ideal candidates for both simultaneous testing and light-guiding applications in MCMs.
poled polyimids are excellent materials for MCM-D applications.
poled polyimids are a viable technology for simultaneous testing of MCM-Ds and optical waveguides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electro-optic polymeric materials are a very useful tool for measuring electric field strength in MCM-D structures.
doped and poles polyimide layers are useful for both simultaneous electrical and optical measurements, and for building optical waveguide interconnects on MCM-D substrates.

the electro-optic properties of poled polymeric films are useful for nondestructive measurement of electric fields in multichip modules, while the optical properties of dopped and poled films make them useful in optical waveguide applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the optical and electro-optic characteristics of doped and polied polyimides can be tailored by the choice of dopant, the dopant level, the poling voltage and time, the poling temperature and time, and the post-poling thermal history.
the electro-optic properties of doped polyimide are sufficiently robust to be used as a nondestructive measurement tool in MCM-D applications.
